chapter: Capitol Records and "On the Street Where You Live"
title: "Baubles, Bangles and Beads" outsells the first hit; vocals; Jumping with Jonah
summary: Cavanaugh handed him "Baubles, Bangles and Beads", a waltz he did not know, and he swung it into a bigger hit; he sang "Just My Luck" and earlier songs, and Jumping with Jonah sold over 500,000.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Well, the next album we come up with, Dave comes back and says, 'We're going to make an album called

Swinging on Broadway." Now it's got all show tunes in there, and he brought out a number and he said, "Now, this is going to be the featured number in here. This is Baubles, Bangles and Beads." Well, I never heard of, "Baubles, Bangles and Beads." So he passed out the piano copy, he give us all four the piano copy, and I said, "Well, I've got to transpose mine a note higher." Okay, but it's a waltz. He said, "Yeah, but swing it, like you did 'On the Street Where You Live,' and get a head introduction and play the first chorus straight and jazz the second chorus," which I did, and this son of a gun was bigger than On the Street.
Yeah, it was bigger than, "On the Street Where You Live," sure.
And didn't you sing one of them?

I sang one, yeah. On that one I sang -- in Swinging on Broadway I sang, "Just My Luck," from the show, "Body Beautiful." But on the first album, Muted Jazz, I sang, "My Blue Heaven," and, "Mack the Knife," and, "St. James Infirmary."
I did three on there. And then we come back and we did Jumping with Jonah, which sold good. Sold over 500,000 albums.
